definition.simple: A natural dye that is used as a color-changing paper to test if something is an acid or a base.
definition.academic: A natural dye extracted from lichens, used as the most common indicator. It turns red in acidic solutions and blue in basic solutions.

common_misconceptions: Litmus is a man-made chemical. (Correction: It is naturally extracted from lichens, which are living organisms.)
ai_context.tutor_hint: Use the memory trick: 'Blue to Red is Acid (BRA), Red to Blue is Base (RBB)' to help remember the color changes.
